newsitem.title: HONG KONG: The worst of Hong Kong fires.
newsitem.headline: The worst of Hong Kong fires.

text.p: The blaze that engulfed a Hong Kong building on Wednesday was the worst in a building on record in the British colony, but not the first to claim a heavy death toll. Here is a list of major fires in the territory's history.

1918 - In the worst fire on record, an estimated 600 people are killed and 400 injured at the Happy Valley racecourse on Hong Kong Island when a grandstand collapsed and food stall stoves were knocked over, setting bamboo matting ablaze.
1929 - A blaze in the Prince Edward Hotel in Hong Kong's Island's Central district kills nine people
1947 - The Canton steamer S.S. Sai On is destroyed by fire on the Hong Kong dockside, killing 149 people.

1953 - On Christmas Day, the Shek Pik Mei squatter village burns down, leaving more than 60,000 homeless. There are no records of the exact numbers living there and the death toll is unknown. The blaze prompted a drive to end squatting by building cheap public housing, in which 3.5 million people now live.
1972 - The cruise liner Queen Elizabeth, serving as a floating university, burns and sinks in Hong Kong harbour, with no casualties.
1986 - Fire guts Chu Ku Tsai village on the Chinese Lunar New Year holiday, leaving 2,000 homeless.
1986 - Fourteen people are killed in a blaze at a fur factory in the Kwai Chung port district.
1986 - A Christmas blaze guts 150 vessels moored in Aberdeen typhoon shelter on Hong Kong Island, leaving more than 1,700 boat dwellers homeless and virtually penniless. But only two are injured.
1990 - Triad gangsters fire-bomb a restaurant and majong parlour in Hunghom, killing six and injuring 24.
1990 - Six dead and 50 injured in a fire in a "cage home" slum hostel in Shamshuipo.
1992 - A blaze at the Shek Kong Vietnamese refugee detention centre kills 26 and injures 126.
1994 - A fire bomb at the Shek Pik Mei branch of a Hong Kong bank kills 12 employees.
1996 - A February dry season brush fire traps schoolchildren hiking at Pat Sin Leng in the New Territories. Three pupils and two teachers are killed and many suffer permanent burn injuries.
1996 - On November 20, the Garley Building in Kowloon's Nathan Road tourist shopping street turns into a towering inferno, killing more than 30 people and injuring about 80.
